An Artist (Japanese: Artist) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that debuted in the Generation IV . They are most commonly depicted as old men wearing berets and carrying art supplies. They are similar to the class from . In Generation IV, they use Pokémon that can learn and , such as and , as well as Pokémon related to the arts, such as and .

In Generation V's Battle Subway, some of them specialize in Pokémon resembling decorative art, with many of these being Pokémon.

In Generation VI, female Artists, depicted as young women holding a paintbrush covered in paint, were introduced. Similar to Generation III's Painters, Artists exclusively use . In Double Battles, two Artists, one male and female, form an . 

In Pokémon Sword and Shield, Artists are depicted as deranged men holding clay sculptures. They keep their Pokémon in Great Balls. In the , Artists specialize in a mix of Pokémon and Pokémon that benefit from .

In Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, Artists are depicted as young female graffiti artists wearing gas masks.

==In the manga==
===Pokémon Adventures===
 
==== ====
An Artist appeared as a background character in Deprogramming Porygon-Z, where he was part of a group of people who entered the after Palmer had his assistants open the gates.

==== ====
In Sylveon Enchants, a female Artist was seen in the Mini-game Corner, playing the Tile Puzzle minigame.

This listing is of cards mentioning or featuring Artists in the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

 
 
 

==Trivia==
Artists are often named in reference to real-life artists:
Artist Gough (Japanese: ビンセント Vincent) from Pokémon Black 2 and White 2 uses a Sunflora. This appears to be a reference to 's .
In Pokémon X and Y, the Artists that challenge the all have the first names of famous real-world artists: Georgia (O'Keeffe), Pierre (Renoir), Salvador (Dali), and Vincent (van Gogh). Artist Jasper (Johns) also challenges the player in the Battle Maison.
In Pokémon Sword and Shield, one of the in-game trade NPCs, who uses the model of an Artist is named Kapoor, likely in reference to British artist .
Most Artists in the Battle Maison use color-based names, such as Jade, Sienna, Rusty, etc.
In , , Artist William's name changes to Kevin in the rematches against him.
